summary: First-iteration full-stack test of RetOps MVP. Seeded a test user+session directly via mongosh, ran 18 pytest cases against public backend URL (all 18 PASSED) and drove the UI via Playwright with session_token cookie. Health, auth exchange rejection, /auth/me, all protected endpoints 401 guard, seed-demo, interactions CRUD + filters (churn_risk, agent_type), rescore, dashboard stats (all 12 keys + sorted top_agents), accounts/agents enrichment, coaching list, playbook (Acme Corp + 404 for missing), settings roundtrip, and MongoDB _id leak guard — all pass. UI: landing renders with RetOps hero + Sign in with Google CTA, /dashboard redirects to /login when unauth, loads full dashboard (coverage 100%, revenue $14.4K at risk, top performers, live alerts) after cookie injection, sidebar navigation works across all 9 routes, Upload -> sample load -> Score redirects to /dashboard/interactions/int_* with rubric + coaching card + save playbook, All Interactions filters (filter-risk, filter-agent-type) populated, row click navigates to detail, Settings save shows 'Settings saved' toast.

ui_bugs.issue: All 7 rubric items render the same 'Marginal' label regardless of item score (e.g. 3/10, 7/10, 9/10 all shown as Marginal). Likely a static tag not derived from score.
Fallback scorer emits suspiciously linear 3,4,5,6,7,8,9 per-item scores for seeded Acme Corp interaction — looks like index values. Functional but not realistic for a demo.

issues: Document <title> is still 'Emergent | Fullstack App' instead of 'RetOps' — update public/index.html title.
Repeated ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED console errors (likely hot-reload websocket in preview). Non-blocking but noisy.

action_items: Update <title> in /app/frontend/public/index.html from 'Emergent | Fullstack App' to 'RetOps'
InteractionDetail.jsx: map rubric tag ('Excellent/Good/Marginal/Poor') from each item's score instead of a constant value
Consider making the deterministic fallback rubric scores less linear (currently look like enumerated index values)
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 334: 'created_at' is stored as ISO string; count_documents uses string >= comparison — works only because ISO-8601 strings are lexicographically ordered. Acceptable but fragile.

server.py dashboard_stats: uses next() picking first all_docs match per account without sorting by created_at, could return a stale interaction. Works here because list_interactions sort orders by created_at desc but not guaranteed in stats path.
server.py is 519 lines — acceptable; splitting into routers/ by domain would improve maintainability as it grows.
require_user reads cookie OR Authorization header correctly and excludes _id — good.
All list endpoints project _id out (projection {_id:0}) — no ObjectId leaks confirmed by recursive test.
CORS allow_credentials=True with allow_origins='*' — browsers will reject credentials with wildcard; set explicit origin in prod.
